So this one is going to be a little different in that I am starting it with an anecdote.

Not long ago a distressed 20-something woman came into my place of business and asked me if I had any exterior camera coverage of the adjoining parking lot. I apologized and told her that I did not. After I asked why she told me that someone had hit her car while she was out and she was hoping I had evidence. I wondered why she needed the footage and asked her if the person had run off without exchanging information. She told me no. Perplexed I asked her if she had called the police. She answered in the affirmative and then explained why she was so distressed. It turns out that the responding officer was friends with the accused and upon arrival to the scene the officer determined that the woman's car was not hit, but instead that she had backed into the police officer's friend's car. Convenient. Now I have seen this kind of thing before and honestly didn't think too much about it, cops playing by a different set of rules seems par for the course for us libertarians; But on her way out this woman who did not seem the sort to consider politics in any way, let alone libertarianism, responded to me with a sentence that gave me chills. She looked me in the eye and said "Is this the system that we are supposed to live in?" I was completely taken aback. She didn't say "Do you believe this asshole, covering for his friend." She didn't say "These [city] police are idiots." She confided in me, a complete stranger, her distrust of the "system" that we live in. Now it may be nothing, I may very well be reading too much into this but to me that response said something about the undercurrent of America. The zeitgeist of the average person. So I ask of you, /v/libertarian. Do you think that the public tide is turning against the police and their impunity to the law? Or will the current spotlight on law enforcement be covered yet again in society's fog?
